podcast.title: Shared Rehab Experience with Scott Weiland (Pre-2003)
podcast.body: Scott Weiland trusted Matt Sorum partly because they had been in rehab together, contributing to the initial chemistry and comfort within Velvet Revolver. "Besides, he'd been in rehab with Matt Sorom so he trusted him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Velvet Revolver Formation (2003)
podcast.body: Matt Sorum, as one of the three core Guns N' Roses members, was instrumental in forming Velvet Revolver alongside Duff McKagan and Slash. "It was Duff, Slash, and drummer Matt Sorom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cool and Friendly Demeanor (2004)
podcast.body: At a press conference for Velvet Revolver's "Contraband" album, Matt Sorum, along with Duff McKagan and Slash, were noted as being "cool, all very friendly, all hanging out together," contrasting with Scott Weiland's detached presence. "The three guns and roses guys were cool, all very friendly, all hanging out together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Brother's Death (March 2007)
podcast.body: Matt Sorum's younger brother passed away from brain cancer in the first week of March 2007, marking a rough start to the year for Velvet Revolver. "Former Matt Sorum's little brother died of brain cancer the first week of March."

xref.title: Formation as a Supergroup (2003)
xref.body: Formed in 2003, Velvet Revolver began with former Guns N' Roses members Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum, who then recruited Dave Kushner from Wasted Youth. They auditioned several singers, including Josh Todd of Buckcherry, Travis Meeks of Days of the New, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, before settling on Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Former Members Form Velvet Revolver (2003)
xref.body: Three former members of Guns N' Roses – Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum – reconciled and formed a new band, Velvet Revolver, in 2003, eventually recruiting Dave Kushner and Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band. It was Duff, Slash, and drummer Matt Sorom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Recruitment into Velvet Revolver (2003)
xref.body: Dave Kushner, formerly of the band Wasted Youth, was convinced by Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum to join their new band, Velvet Revolver, as they sought a singer. "Plus they had convinced their buddy Dave Kushner for a band called Wasted Youth to join up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Scott Weiland's Initial Reluctance and Trust (2003)
xref.body: Scott Weiland initially disliked the music presented by the band, but a second demo convinced him to jam. He showed up late due to drug use, but found unexpected chemistry and a low ego factor, particularly trusting Matt Sorum due to a shared rehab experience. "Matt, to Scott's surprise, the ego factor was low and the chemistry was bang on. Besides, he'd been in rehab with Matt Sorom so he trusted him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Velvet Revolver Audition and Trust (2003)
xref.body: Scott Weiland initially disliked the music sent by the future Velvet Revolver members but agreed to jam after hearing a second, improved CD. Despite arriving hours late due to drug use, he found the chemistry with Duff McKagan, Slash, Matt Sorum, and Dave Kushner to be "bang on" and trusted Matt Sorum from a shared rehab experience. "Besides, he'd been in rehab with Matt Sorom so he trusted him."

xref.title: Rough Start to 2007
xref.body: The year 2007 began difficult for the band with the death of Matt Sorum's younger brother from brain cancer in early March, followed by the death of Scott Weiland's younger brother, Michael, a month later. "Things started off rough for Velvara Volver in 2007. Former Matt Sorum's little brother died of brain cancer the first week of March."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Final Texts and Plans (July 2017)
xref.body: In July 2017, while his wife Talinda and six children were on vacation in Arizona, Chester Bennington returned to Los Angeles on July 19, citing a television commercial shoot as the reason. Around the same time, he exchanged texts with Robert DeLeo of Stone Temple Pilots and Matt Sorum of Guns N' Roses, even floating the idea of performing with Sorum again in their band Kings of Chaos, with no alarm bells raised by anyone. "In July 2017, his wife, Talinda, and his family, he had six kids, went to Arizona on a vacation. But then on July 19th, he said he had to get back to LA."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Proposed Reformation (2017)
xref.body: On July 19, 2017, Chester Bennington sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer of Guns N' Roses, expressing his enthusiasm for reforming Kings of Chaos, which he described as an "all-star covers band." This communication occurred less than 24 hours before Chester's death. "On July 19, he sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer with guns and roses, saying that he would like to reform kings of chaos and all-star covers band. That'd be so much fun, he said."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Final Interactions and Plans
xref.body: On July 14, 2017, Chester filmed "Carpool Karaoke" looking great. On July 18, he spoke with longtime friend Sean Doudel of Gray Days, sounding great, and was later seen laughing and joking with his family in a video. On July 19, he emailed Matt Sorum about reforming the all-star covers band Kings of Chaos, expressing excitement. "On July 19, he sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer with guns and roses, saying that he would like to reform kings of chaos and all-star covers band. That'd be so much fun, he said."

xref.title: Video Appearance
xref.body: Slash, Duff McKagan, and Matt Sorum from Guns N' Roses and Velvet Revolver made an appearance in The Strokes' music video for their song "Someday," the third single from their debut album "Is This It." "They even had Slash, Duff McKagan and Matt Soren from Guns and Roses and Velvet Revolver appear in their video."

xref.title: Video Appearance
xref.body: Slash, Duff McKagan, and Matt Sorum, who were also members of Velvet Revolver (and Guns N' Roses), appeared in The Strokes' music video for "Someday." This collaboration was noted as a significant endorsement for the emerging band. "They even had Slash, Duff McKagan and Matt Soren from Guns and Roses and Velvet Revolver appear in their video."
